title: Locomotion and Movement
syllabus: Types of movement - ciliary, flagellar, amoeboid, muscular; Skeletal muscle - contractile proteins and muscle contraction; Skeletal system and its functions; Joints; Disorders of muscular and skeletal system - Myasthenia gravis, Tetany, Muscular dystrophy, Arthritis, Osteoporosis, Gout.

questions.question: Which of the following cellular structures or cell types exhibit amoeboid movement in the human body?
options: Ciliated epithelial cells of the trachea
questions.solution: Some specialized cells in our body like macrophages and leukocytes in blood exhibit amoeboid movement. It is effected by pseudopodia formed by the streaming of protoplasm, and microfilaments of the cytoskeleton are also involved.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of movement and their anatomical occurrences:

List-I (Type of Movement)List-II (Site / Example)
(A) Amoeboid(I) Passage of ova through female reproductive tract
(B) Ciliary(II) Movement of jaws, limbs, and tongue
(C) Flagellar(III) Macrophages and neutrophils
(D) Muscular(IV) Swimming of spermatozoa

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Amoeboid movement is seen in macrophages and neutrophils; Ciliary movement helps in the passage of ova in the fallopian tubes and mucus in the respiratory tract; Flagellar movement helps in the swimming of spermatozoa; Muscular movement is involved in movement of limbs, jaws, tongue, etc.

questions.question: The functional unit of contraction in a skeletal muscle fibre situated between two successive Z-lines is called a:
questions.solution: The portion of the myofibril between two successive 'Z' lines is considered as the functional unit of contraction and is called a sarcomere.

questions.question: Each thin filament (actin filament) is composed of two 'F' (filamentous) actins helically wound to each other. Two filaments of another protein, ________, also run close to the 'F' actin throughout its length:
questions.solution: Two filaments of tropomyosin also run close to the 'F' actin throughout its length. In the resting state, a complex protein troponin is distributed at regular intervals on the tropomyosin, masking the active binding sites for myosin on actin filaments.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the components of the Myosin (thick) filament:

List-I (Component)List-II (Feature / Binding Site)
(A) Heavy Meromyosin (HMM)(I) Linear tail portion of the monomer
(B) Light Meromyosin (LMM)(II) Globular head with a short arm (cross-arm)
(C) Globular Head(III) Active ATPase enzyme, ATP binding site, and actin binding site

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Each meromyosin has two parts: Heavy Meromyosin (HMM) which includes the globular head and short arm, and Light Meromyosin (LMM) which is the tail. The globular head functions as an active ATPase enzyme and has binding sites for ATP and active sites for actin.

questions.question: During skeletal muscle contraction according to the Sliding Filament Theory, which of the following bands/zones SHORTENS while another remains constant in length?
options: I-band and H-zone shorten, while A-band retains its length
A-band and I-band shorten, while H-zone remains constant
A-band shortens, while I-band retains its length
Z-line expands, while I-band and A-band shorten
questions.solution: During contraction, the thin actin filaments slide over the thick myosin filaments towards the centre of the A-band. Consequently, the I-bands shorten, the H-zone narrows or disappears, and the A-band retains its original length.

questions.question: Upon stimulation by a motor nerve impulse, which ion is released from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the sarcoplasm to initiate cross-bridge cycling?
questions.solution: An action potential in the sarcolemma spreads through the T-tubules and causes the release of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ ions from the sarcoplasmic reticulum into the sarcoplasm. $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ binds to a subunit of troponin (Troponin-C), causing a conformational change that unmasks the active sites on actin for myosin.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding muscle fibers:
Statement I: Red muscle fibers contain abundant myoglobin and numerous mitochondria, relying primarily on aerobic oxidation.
Statement II: White muscle fibers contain low myoglobin, fewer mitochondria, but a high amount of sarcoplasmic reticulum, relying on anaerobic glycolysis.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Red muscle fibers (slow-twitch) are rich in myoglobin and mitochondria, facilitating sustained aerobic work. White muscle fibers (fast-twitch) have less myoglobin and fewer mitochondria but a well-developed sarcoplasmic reticulum for rapid anaerobic bursts.

questions.question: The human axial skeleton consists of how many total bones distributed along the main longitudinal axis of the body?
questions.solution: The human skeleton consists of 206 bones divided into: Axial skeleton (80 bones: skull, vertebral column, sternum, ribs) and Appendicular skeleton (126 bones: limbs and girdles).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the constituent bones of the human skull:

List-I (Skull Region)List-II (Number of Bones)
(A) Cranial bones(I) 14
(B) Facial bones(II) 8
(C) Ear ossicles (in both middle ears)(III) 1
(D) Hyoid bone(IV) 6 (3 in each ear: Malleus, Incus, Stapes)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Cranial bones = 8; Facial bones = 14; Ear ossicles = 6 (Malleus, Incus, Stapes in pairs); Hyoid bone = 1 (U-shaped bone at the base of the buccal cavity). Total skull bones (including ossicles and hyoid) = 29.

questions.question: The human skull is described as 'dicondylic' because it articulates with the superior region of the vertebral column (atlas vertebra) with the help of:
questions.solution: The human skull articulates with the superior region of the vertebral column with the help of two occipital condyles, hence it is termed a dicondylic skull.

questions.question: The human vertebral column is formed by 26 serially arranged units called vertebrae. The correct formula representing the regional distribution of vertebrae starting from the cranial end is:
questions.solution: The number of vertebrae are: Cervical (7), Thoracic (12), Lumbar (5), Sacral (1, fused from 5), and Coccygeal (1, fused from 4), designated as $\text{C}_7 \text{Th}_{12} \text{L}_5 \text{S}_{(1)} \text{Co}_{(1)}$.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the classification of human Ribs:

List-I (Rib Category)List-II (Pairs & Attachment Feature)
(A) True ribs (Vertebrosternal)(I) 8th, 9th, and 10th pairs; attach to 7th rib hyaline cartilage (Vertebrochondral)
(B) False ribs(II) 11th and 12th pairs; not connected ventrally (Floating ribs)
(C) Floating ribs (Vertebral)(III) 1st to 7th pairs; attached dorsally to thoracic vertebrae and ventrally to sternum

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: True ribs (1st-7th pairs): Vertebrosternal, connected to sternum by hyaline cartilage; False ribs (8th, 9th, 10th pairs): Vertebrochondral, articulate with 7th rib; Floating ribs (11th and 12th pairs): Vertebral, unattached ventrally.

questions.question: A flat triangular bone located in the dorsal part of the thorax between the second and seventh ribs is the:
questions.solution: The scapula (shoulder blade) is a large, triangular, flat bone situated on the dorsal surface of the rib cage between the second and the seventh ribs.

questions.question: The glenoid cavity is an anatomical depression present on the pectoral girdle that articulates with the:
options: Head of the humerus to form the shoulder joint
Head of the femur to form the hip joint
questions.solution: Below the acromion process of the scapula is a shallow depression called the glenoid cavity which articulates with the head of the humerus to form the ball-and-socket shoulder joint.

questions.question: Each coxal (hip) bone of the pelvic girdle is formed by the fusion of which three bones?
questions.solution: Each coxal bone is formed by the fusion of three bones: Ilium, Ischium, and Pubis. At the point of fusion of these three bones is a cup-shaped cavity called the acetabulum, with which the thigh bone (femur) articulates.

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the types of Synovial Joints and their anatomical examples:

List-I (Joint Type)List-II (Location in Human Body)
(A) Ball and socket joint(I) Knee joint / Elbow joint
(B) Hinge joint(II) Between Atlas and Axis vertebrae
(C) Pivot joint(III) Between Humerus and Pectoral girdle (glenoid cavity)
(D) Gliding joint(IV) Between Carpal and Metacarpal of thumb
(E) Saddle joint(V) Between the adjacent Carpals in the wrist

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Ball and socket: Shoulder and hip joints; Hinge: Knee, elbow, interphalangeal joints; Pivot: Between atlas and axis; Gliding: Between adjacent carpals; Saddle: Between carpal and metacarpal of thumb.

questions.question: Fibrous joints (synarthroses) are immovable joints characterized by dense fibrous connective tissue. A classic example is:
options: Sutures between flat bones of the cranium
Joint between carpal and metacarpal of thumb
questions.solution: Fibrous joints do not allow any movement. This type of joint is shown by the flat skull bones which fuse end-to-end with the help of dense fibrous connective tissues in the form of sutures to form the cranium.

questions.question: Cartilaginous joints, in which bones are joined together with the help of cartilage permitting limited movement, are found:
options: Between adjacent vertebrae in the vertebral column and pubic symphysis
Between frontal and parietal cranial bones
questions.solution: In cartilaginous joints, bones are joined by white fibrocartilage or hyaline cartilage, allowing limited flexibility (e.g., intervertebral discs between adjacent vertebrae and the pubic symphysis of the pelvic girdle).

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II regarding the disorders of the Muscular and Skeletal systems:

List-I (Disorder)List-II (Pathological Feature / Cause)
(A) Myasthenia gravis(I) Wild sustained contractions (spasms) due to low $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ in body fluids
(B) Muscular dystrophy(II) Autoimmune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction leading to fatigue and paralysis
(C) Tetany(III) Age-related decrease in bone mass and high fracture risk associated with low estrogen
(D) Osteoporosis(IV) Progressive genetic degeneration of skeletal muscle (X-linked recessive)
(E) Gout(V) Inflammation of joints due to accumulation of uric acid crystals

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution: Myasthenia gravis: Autoimmune disease attacking ACh receptors; Muscular dystrophy: Genetic degenerative disease (e.g., Duchenne muscular dystrophy); Tetany: Muscle spasms due to hypocalcemia; Osteoporosis: Decreased bone density from estrogen decline in postmenopausal females; Gout: Uric acid crystal deposits in joint cavities.

questions.question: The central lighter region of the A-band that contains only thick myosin filaments and is not overlapped by thin actin filaments in resting state is called the:
questions.solution: In the resting state, the edges of thin filaments on either side of thick filaments partially overlap the free ends of thick filaments. The central part of the thick filament, not overlapped by thin filaments, is called the 'H' zone.

questions.question: The thin elastic fibrous membrane that holds thick myosin filaments together in the middle of the H-zone is the:
questions.solution: The thick filaments in the 'A' band are held together in the middle of this band by a thin fibrous membrane called the 'M' line.

questions.question: Which of the following bones is a sesamoid bone developed by the ossification within a tendon?
questions.solution: The patella is a cup-shaped sesamoid bone that covers the knee joint ventrally, formed by ossification within the tendon of the quadriceps femoris muscle.

questions.question: Each human forelimb contains 30 bones. The correct count of carpals (wrist bones), metacarpals (palm bones), and phalanges (digits) in one forelimb is:
questions.solution: Each forelimb consists of: Humerus (1), Radius (1), Ulna (1), Carpals (wrist bones = 8), Metacarpals (palm bones = 5), and Phalanges (digits = 14 with formula 2, 3, 3, 3, 3). Total = 30.

questions.question: Each human hindlimb contains 30 bones. The count of tarsals (ankle bones) in one hindlimb is:
questions.solution: Each hindlimb contains: Femur (1), Patella (1), Tibia (1), Fibula (1), Tarsals (ankle bones = 7), Metatarsals (5), and Phalanges (14). Total = 30 bones.

questions.question:
Read the following statements regarding the clavicle (collar bone):
Statement I: Each clavicle is a long, slender S-shaped bone with two curvatures.
Statement II: The clavicle articulates laterally with the acromion process of the scapula.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Each clavicle is a slender S-shaped bone with two curvatures that articulates with the sternum medially and the acromion of the scapula laterally.

questions.question: The junction between a motor neuron and the sarcolemma of a muscle fiber is called the neuromuscular junction or:
questions.solution: A neural signal reaching the neuromuscular junction (or motor end-plate) releases a neurotransmitter (acetylcholine), which generates an action potential in the sarcolemma.

questions.question: A motor neuron along with all the muscle fibers it innervates constitutes a:
questions.solution: A motor unit is composed of a single somatic motor neuron and all the muscle fibers (muscle cells) innervated by its terminal axon branches.

questions.question: Which of the following events triggers the detachment of the myosin head from the actin binding site during the cross-bridge cycle?
options: Binding of a new ATP molecule to the myosin head
Hydrolysis of ATP into ADP and Pi
Efflux of $\text{K}^+$ ions out of sarcolemma
questions.solution: After the power stroke, the release of ADP and Pi allows a new ATP molecule to bind to the myosin head, breaking the cross-bridge and detaching myosin from actin. Hydrolysis of this ATP then re-energizes the head for the next cycle.

questions.question: Accumulation of lactic acid due to anaerobic breakdown of glycogen in muscle fibers during repeated strenuous activity leads to:
questions.solution: Repeated activation of muscles can lead to the accumulation of lactic acid due to anaerobic breakdown of glycogen, causing muscle fatigue.

questions.question: The acromion process is a prominent expansion of the elevated ridge (spine) of the:
questions.solution: The scapula has a sharp ridge (spine) on its dorsal side which projects as an expanded process called the acromion. The clavicle articulates with this acromion process.

questions.question: Which of the following vertebrae provides articulation with the occipital condyles of the skull and facilitates the 'nodding' movement of the head?
questions.solution: The first cervical vertebra is the atlas. It articulates with the occipital condyles of the skull via its superior articular facets, forming the atlanto-occipital joint for nodding ('yes') movements.

questions.question: The pivot joint that allows the rotational 'side-to-side' ('no') movement of the head is situated between the:
questions.solution: The pivot joint (atlanto-axial joint) is located between the atlas (C1) and the odontoid process of the axis (C2), allowing horizontal rotational movement of the head.

questions.question: The rib cage in humans is formed by:
options: 12 pairs of ribs, 12 thoracic vertebrae, and 1 sternum
10 pairs of ribs and scapula only
questions.solution: Thoracic vertebrae (12), ribs (12 pairs = 24), and sternum (1) together form the thoracic cage (rib cage) protecting the heart and lungs.

questions.question: Osteoporosis is a common age-related skeletal disease characterized by decreased bone mineral density and increased fragility. A major contributing physiological factor in postmenopausal females is:
questions.solution: Osteoporosis is an age-related disorder characterized by decreased bone mass and increased risk of fractures. Decreased levels of estrogen after menopause is a common cause.

questions.question: The two halves of the pelvic girdle meet ventrally to form the pubic symphysis containing:
questions.solution: The two halves of the pelvic girdle meet ventrally to form the pubic symphysis containing white fibrous cartilage.

questions.question: Arthritis is defined pathologically as:
questions.solution: Arthritis is a general term denoting the inflammation of one or more joints, leading to pain, swelling, and stiffness (e.g., osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis).

questions.question: Gouty arthritis (gout) is caused by the deposition of which crystals in and around synovial joints?
questions.solution: Gout is the inflammation of joints due to the accumulation and crystallization of uric acid (monosodium urate crystals) within synovial joint cavities.

questions.question: Which of the following is a genetic disorder characterized by progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle fibers, mostly inherited as an X-linked recessive trait?
questions.solution: Muscular dystrophy is a progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle mostly due to genetic defect (e.g., mutation in the dystrophin gene). Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder.

questions.question: In the resting state of skeletal muscle, the active myosin-binding sites on actin are masked by:
questions.solution: In resting muscle, the troponin subunit (Troponin-I) along with tropomyosin covers and masks the active myosin-binding sites on actin subunits, preventing premature cross-bridge formation.

questions.question: The storehouse of calcium ions in a skeletal muscle fiber is the:
questions.solution: The sarcoplasmic reticulum of muscle fibers is a modified smooth endoplasmic reticulum that acts as the intracellular reservoir and storehouse of calcium ions ($\text{Ca}^{2+}$).

questions.question: Each skeletal muscle in our body is made of many muscle bundles or fascicles held together by a common collagenous connective tissue sheath called:
questions.solution: Each organized skeletal muscle consists of several muscle bundles (fascicles) held together by a common collagenous connective tissue layer called fascia.

questions.question: Synovial joints are characterized by the presence of a fluid-filled synovial cavity between articulating surfaces of two bones. The synovial fluid functions to:
options: Lubricate the joint, reduce friction, and nourish articular cartilage
Lock the joint to prevent all movements
Transmit electrical nerve impulses across bones
questions.solution: Synovial joints have a synovial cavity filled with viscous, hyaluronic acid-rich synovial fluid that lubricates the articulating hyaline cartilage surfaces, minimizing friction and allowing smooth movement.

questions.question: Tetany is caused by:
options: Hypocalcemia (low calcium ion level in extracellular body fluids)
questions.solution: Tetany is characterized by rapid spasms (wild sustained contractions) in muscles due to low $\text{Ca}^{2+}$ in body fluid (hypocalcemia, often secondary to hypoparathyroidism).

questions.question:
Read the following statements:
Statement I: Ciliary movement in the human body helps remove dust particles inhaled into the trachea and transports ova through the female reproductive tract.
Statement II: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disease where antibodies target acetylcholine receptors at the neuromuscular junction.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.solution: Both statements are correct according to NCERT. Coordinated ciliary movements clear foreign matter from the respiratory tract and propel ova along the fallopian tubes. Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder that damages nicotinic acetylcholine receptors at the motor end-plate, resulting in progressive muscle weakness and paralysis.
